researcher: Codex parallel americas-powers-seventeen-first research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Crow Tribe Tourism Office: Culture
sources.note: Direct page read. Use community self-name, living culture and explicitly oral migration tradition only. Do not adopt its questionable IRA chronology or exact horse-acquisition year.

sources.title: Little Big Horn College: Archaeology of the Apsáalooke People
sources.note: Full indexed original text. Queries site:lib2.lbhc.edu "Archaeology of the Apsáalooke" "1725" and site:lib2.lbhc.edu "Hagen" "corn" expose relevant paragraphs; direct fetch fails. Horse estimate circa 1725 differs from tourism 1735, so broad early eighteenth century used.

sources.title: Dale D. Old Horn and Timothy P. McCleary: History and Meaning of the Tipi
sources.note: Full indexed original adaptation of Apsáalooke Social and Family Structure, Little Big Horn College, 1995. Opening ashé / home and ashtáale / real home, then poles and smoke flaps. Count together with cr-kin and cr-land as one underlying work.

sources.title: Old Horn and McCleary: The Apsáalooke
sources.note: Full indexed original, 1995 book pages1 to7. Sits In The Middle Land’s 1851 four-pole homeland description. Same-work budget with cr-home and cr-kin.

sources.title: Smithsonian American Art Museum: Apsáalooke Crow Artist’s Dress
sources.note: Direct page lines 209 to 215. Denver Art Museum 1985.46 circa 1930, materials include bone; general elk-tooth tradition can use up to 500 teeth and modern substitutes. Do not claim this particular dress has 500 real teeth.

sources.title: Field Museum: Apsáalooke Women and Warriors
sources.note: Direct institutional 2019 announcement, Nina Sanders curatorship, seven shields, women as keepers, spiritual significance, historic and contemporary art.

sources.title: Community-Based Research to Reduce Environmental Health Disparities
sources.note: Full indexed primary 2015 paper, Crow case study and Approach, committee founded 2005, Crow coordinator and college science majors test water, thirty high-contamination families follow-up. No current universal contamination claim.

sources.title: Little Big Horn College: Kinship Card Game
sources.note: Full indexed original modern grades9 to12 lesson plan, kinship cards and reflection on family relationships. Not an ancient game claim.

sources.title: Fort Belknap Indian Community: History
sources.note: Direct page, Gros Ventre section and shared bison economy. Use documented Saskatchewan contact circa 1754,1876 refusal and 1878 restoration. Exclude erroneous 1826 Maximilian date, questionable 1885 mining cession, general 1855 Fort Laramie wording and Assiniboine-specific customs.

sources.title: Andrew Cowell: The Aaniiih (Gros Ventre) Language
sources.note: Direct university-press account of 2024 reference grammar: Algonquian, close Arapaho relationship, historic central/southern Alberta/Saskatchewan and north Montana, community revitalization.

sources.title: Montana Office of Public Instruction: Traditional Games Model Lesson Plan
sources.note: Full indexed original, station2 Gros Ventre (White Clay) shinny. Buffalo-hair stuffing and stitched buckskin; figure 799 from 1907 Bureau of American Ethnology report, Field Museum 60356. Text and figure dimensions conflict, so no size claim.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Parfleche Case Model
sources.note: Full indexed museum object record27/213: Chandler Good Strike,1999 Fort Belknap; rawhide, paint, wool felt, synthetic fabric; folded, painted, tied.

sources.title: English - Gros Ventre/White Clay Student Dictionary
sources.note: Direct54-page PDF text. Title page credits Andrew Cowell with Terry Brockie and John Stiff Arm,2012, based on Allan Taylor’s 1960s to 1990s work. Printed25/PDF index24 exact house, home: báyaaah. Some other entries have failed font extraction, so use intact entry only; screenshot failed.

sources.title: Institute of Museum and Library Services: Fort Belknap 2012 Library Grant
sources.note: Full indexed original grant abstract. Proposed permission requests for twenty children’s books, committee translations and transparent printed labels. Future/planned wording preserved; no unsupported completion claim.

sources.title: Aaniiih Nakoda College: History
sources.note: Direct official college history,1983 charter,2011 renaming,1993 accreditation. Distinct from older external source saying 1984.

sources.title: Confluence for Climate Education: Aaniiih Nakoda College
sources.note: Direct 2021 account of college programs, mosquito monitoring by environmental science/allied health students and Milk River organism study by instructor Dan Kinsey. Author describes college’s own work; no medical advice.

sources.title: Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute: Tribal Bison Restoration Study
sources.note: Full indexed institutional 2022 research announcement quoting Fort Belknap Buffalo Program’s Bronc Speakthunder: reintroduction late 1970s. Four tribal case studies, ecological/food-sovereignty objectives. Shared Fort Belknap program includes both nations.

sources.title: Little Big Horn College, Tribal Histories Project, Introduction
sources.note: Bands, seasonal movements, stored foods and Crow Fair; college community history.

sources.title: Little Big Horn College, Kinship
sources.note: Matrilineal clans, extended family terminology and responsibility for children.

sources.title: Patrick J. Hill and Timothy P. McCleary, Apsáalooke warrior’s exploit robe, NMAI
sources.note: Catalogue 1/2558, approximately 1850; materials, collecting in 1861 and narrative writing interpretation.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Tipi liner, 18/9242
sources.note: Materials, techniques and collection history; acquired in 1936, earlier provenance unknown.

sources.title: Little Big Horn College, Early Reservation
sources.note: Winter of 1883 to 1884, school separation and Crow adaptations of house plans and liners. Its erroneous 1880 Dawes Act date is not adopted.

sources.title: Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks, Chief Plenty Coups State Park
sources.note: Preserved home, store and farm, occupied from 1884 until Plenty Coups’ death in 1932.

sources.title: Treaty with the Crows, 1868, Little Big Horn College transcription
sources.note: Signing date and articles II and IV; historical reservation and hunting provisions, not advice on current law.

sources.title: Crow Tribe Executive Branch, official government website
sources.note: General Council section describes the 2001 Constitution and three branches of tribal government.

sources.title: Smithsonian Recovering Voices, Apsáalooke: Revitalizing the Past, Formatting for the 21st Century
sources.note: Community research visit in March 2016; object study, recordings and planned digital resources, distinguished from completed products.

sources.title: Montana DNRC, Fort Belknap Indian Reservation setting
sources.note: Historical background on the 1855 territory, establishment of the reservation in 1888 and later land loss; no advice about current legal rights.

sources.title: A. L. Kroeber, Ethnology of the Gros Ventre, 1908
sources.note: Pages 145, 149, 150, 162 and 164. Mostly community testimony gathered in 1901; the author’s cultural rankings and predictions of disappearance are rejected.

sources.title: Clarena Brockie, testimony to the US Senate, 2014
sources.note: Printed pages 28 to 33, immersion school opening in 2003, teaching practices and assimilation. Conflicting college-charter wording is excluded.

sources.title: Defenders of Wildlife, Yellowstone bison arrive at Fort Belknap, August 2013
sources.note: Participating organisation’s account of the August 2013 transfer and its intended cultural and ecological purposes.

sources.title: US Fish and Wildlife Service, Fort Belknap buffalo restoration and grazing system
sources.note: Fiscal 2024 funded project description. Proposed fencing and water systems are not reported as completed construction.
